subject.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown

question: Should the gateway’s terminal CLI owner force-exit five seconds after a completed shutdown when residual event-loop handles remain, with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_POST_SHUTDOWN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS` as the operator override?
rationale: This is an intentional availability-versus-graceful-cleanup and environment-surface contract, not a mechanical defect that review automation can safely choose.

options.title: Accept the watchdog contract
options.body: Land the terminal-owned watchdog and strict internal health probe after the current-head checks pass, accepting forced exit as the supervisor-availability safeguard.

options.title: Remove the override surface
options.body: Keep the recovery design but replace the public environment override with a maintainer-owned fixed policy if the additional operator knob is not acceptable.

options.title: Pause for a different recovery design
options.body: Do not merge the force-exit behavior if gateway owners require a supervisor-only or otherwise narrower recovery mechanism.

recommendation.title: Accept the watchdog contract
recommendation.body: Land the terminal-owned watchdog and strict internal health probe after the current-head checks pass, accepting forced exit as the supervisor-availability safeguard.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person most directly to the gateway HTTP and restart paths whose lifecycle contract changes here.
